title: Man Held After Shootout in Delhi Park Gang-Rape by Fake Cops; Two at Large
excerpt: A teenage girl was allegedly assaulted at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir on Monday; one accused was shot in the leg during his arrest, two others are being hunted.
body:
• Three men posing as policemen allegedly gang-raped a teenage girl at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in south Delhi on Monday evening.
  • One of the accused, identified as Asif, was arrested after an exchange of fire with police; he was shot in the leg and is being treated at AIIMS Trauma Centre.
  • Two other accused remain at large, and police are scanning CCTV footage from the area to trace them.
  • A case has been registered under the POCSO Act, and the survivor's statement has been recorded.

What happened on Monday evening

The girl, described by police as 17 years old — some initial reports put her age at 16 — had visited the Kalkaji Mandir with a male friend at around 7 pm on Monday. After offering prayers, the two walked to nearby Astha Kunj Park, close to the temple and the ISKCON Temple, at about 7:30 pm. There, three men aged roughly 25 to 30 approached them claiming to be policemen, according to the complaint.

The men allegedly questioned and threatened the teenagers, exploiting the authority of the uniforms they claimed to wear. According to the girl's statement, one of the accused restrained her friend while the others assaulted her, before threatening both teenagers and leaving the park. A PCR call reporting the assault was received at 8:45 pm, police said. Officers reached the spot, took the girl for a medical examination and recorded her statement. A case was registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

The arrest after an exchange of fire

On Tuesday, Delhi Police arrested one of the three accused, identified as Asif, following a brief encounter in southeast Delhi. According to PTI, Asif allegedly opened fire — three rounds — when a police team tried to intercept him near DM Office Road in Amar Colony. One bullet struck the bullet-proof jacket of head constable Rajesh; in self-defence, the officer fired two rounds, one of which hit Asif in the right leg, the agency reported.

Asif was moved to the AIIMS Trauma Centre for treatment, and crime and forensic teams were called to the encounter site. Police are scanning CCTV footage from the area around the park to identify and trace the two remaining accused, who are still at large.

A disturbing pattern in ten days

The Kalkaji case is the fourth serious sexual assault involving a minor reported in Delhi in roughly ten days, according to NationPress. On September 16, a sixth-grade girl was sexually assaulted by a 56-year-old shopkeeper, Maqsood, inside a shop in Sadar Bazaar after being lured in and restrained; he was arrested the same day and sent to judicial custody. On September 13, the decomposed body of a teenage gang-rape and murder victim was found in Swaroop Nagar; all four accused, including three juveniles, were arrested.

The recurrence has reignited debate over the safety of women and girls in the capital's public spaces. The impersonation tactic in the Kalkaji case adds a further dimension: by posing as police officers, the accused allegedly weaponized public trust in law enforcement itself to prevent resistance — a compound offence that investigators say raises broader questions about deterrence and patrolling in the city's parks and markets.
